content: A place for town leadership to discuss matters of town business away from the common rabble.

<@&739384242726764586> The quartermaster has finished documenting all the salvaged goods from the wreckage. But there is a problem with the food. Rats and other rodents are eating it! A watch has been set up, but to little effect. It falls on you, leaders of civilization, to take care of this problem. The portions of food set aside for the aristocracy have been protected, but soon the common folk will start going hungry and getting sick. 

Your task is to fund and oversee the construction of a secure storehouse for food and other perishables. **This will cost 5000 gold worth of resources to build, and 10 Labor to complete.** Labor can only be done by Serfs. The food is rotting quickly. If this task is not completed by the end of the day Monday, all non-aristocracy will gain one level of exhaustion until this task is complete. 

(Use the Crafting Tracker to document the Serfs labor. https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1kuaq_hCQEgOwH43rhS6sg3rBgD0FwMWEjcBhL_5_cIo/edit?usp=sharing)
Good Luck!
(We levy a tax. Ezpz.)
That is certainly a possibility.
You may have trouble enforcing it before a mayor is elected, but if you can convince the whole council to agree, the ship's captain may be willing to enforce such a tax.
You could always just choose not to complete it and let the common folk get weak and sick. You have plenty of food and will be fine. The debuf will not affect aristocracy.

How much do we tell to the colony?  Personally I feel it is best to fully inform... but that may cause rioting.... so do we vote on what we tell?"

I would suggest in the meantime we simply request a 150 gold levy to help pay for the silo, with a description of why the building is necessary and what will happen if it is not constructed. 

I suggest we offer citizens who partake in the construction 50 gold a piece for their efforts as a way to incentivize cooperation. In the event that we do not have enough funding, I would suggest each aristocrat here donates to the cause.”

Lt Pandy stops by to thank the council. He is covered in dirt and sweat from working on the structure all day. "Thank you for your efforts in making this secure storage and granary. This is a great first step in getting the colony off on the right foot. I hate to ask more from you, but construction has started on a defensive wall. If you could use your influence to help speed that process along, we will all be saver for it. Thank you again."

(Congratulations! You have shown your willingness to help out the town even when you did not benefit directly. Because of your actions, the common folk will NOT receive a debuff. You are all truly unsung heroes. To contribute to work on the wall, labor must be assigned in the crafting tracker.)

Remember that a charter must be written describing the rules of the town and the function of government powers, voting decisions, term limits, and anything regarding a due process.

What happens if someone is accused of a crime. Who processes it and what are the punishments.

Should cannibalisms be allowed?

What keeps people in checks and balances. 

How are disputes handled and settled?

Project Updates:
- The Storehouse was completed a week ago, avoiding a terrible status for all lowborn folk.
- A giant pile of manure was cleaned up, avoiding the stench that implied. 
- Drinking water supply has been restored.

Attention Mayor and Aristocracy! THE WATER IS RISING!
Merchants have begun reporting to you that their businesses are flooding. If this keeps up, muddy streets will be the least of your worries. The only long term solution seems to be going mobile. It falls to you.

You must convert merchant shops into wagons in case you need to seek higher ground. Converting the shops will cost **20,000 gold** worth of resources, and take **30 labor!** If this is not completed by Thursday, end of day, merchants will no longer be able to craft goods, and current production will be halted. There may be other consequences as well. 

But fear not. This land has been blessed with an ample supply of natives. The crown has granted you authority to conscript labor and collect taxes from these creatures. It may be time to exercise that authority. You may come together as a community and take care of these costs yourselves, or you can force the local natives to do this work for you. (Results may vary depending or RP of your interaction with the natives.)

Good Luck.
